title: Combined Antiplatelet Strategy in Acute Ischemic Stroke Following Thrombectomy and/or Intravenous Thrombolysis (CoPRIME)
official: Combined Antiplatelet Strategy in Acute Ischemic Stroke Following Thrombectomy and/or Intravenous Thrombolysis (CoPRIME): A Randomized Pilot Study (DOMAIN Under ACT-GLOBAL Platform Trial)
summary:
Strokes are an major cause of disability. The most common stroke is called an "ischemic stroke". These strokes happen when a blood vessel in the brain is blocked by a clot. The blockage decreases blood flow. This damages the brain. To treat stroke, doctors use medicines and procedures to remove the clot.

After patients have a stroke, they may have another one in the first few weeks. Doctors often use aspirin to prevent another stroke. However, more strokes might be prevented if we use aspirin together with a medicine called clopidogrel or with ticagrelor. Aspirin plus clopidogrel or aspirin plus ticagrelor might prevent more clots from forming in the blood. The risk of these medicines are bleeding.

This study will test if using aspirin plus clopidogrel or aspirin plus ticagrelor together for 3 weeks is safe and practical when compared to aspirin alone. Patients will have a chance to join the study soon after they have been treated for a stroke. They will be checked for a low risk of bleeding with a brain scan. The study treatment will be chosen by chance like a coin toss. One third will take aspirin alone. One third will take aspirin and clopidogrel. One a third will take aspirin and ticagrelor. The study team will follow participants for three months.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria

1. Participants must be ≥18 years of age at randomization.
2. Acute non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke treated with reperfusion therapy, defined as intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) and/or endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).
3. Time from the end of acute reperfusion therapy to randomization ≤ 30 hours.
4. Mild-to-moderate deficit is defined as a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score ≤10 at the time of randomization.
5. At least one non-contrast CT scan completed post-reperfusion therapy and prior to randomization.
6. Signed informed consent from the patient or surrogate decision maker.

Exclusion criteria

1. Post-reperfusion CT scan shows cerebral parenchymal hematoma (parenchymal hematoma type 1 and 2) or confluent hematoma (Hemorrhagic Infarction type 2). Petechial hemorrhagic transformation (Hemorrhagic Infarction type 1) and contrast staining alone will be included.
2. Any known disorder associated with a significantly increased risk of bleeding.
3. Anticoagulation is required for any indication other than DVT prophylaxis.
4. Evidence-based indication for dual antiplatelet therapy.
5. Planned surgical intervention in the next 30 days includes but is not limited to carotid endarterectomy, where dual antiplatelet therapy is not indicated, and carotid stenting, where single antiplatelet therapy is not used.
6. History of non-traumatic intracranial or subarachnoid hemorrhage within the last 1 year.
7. Intracranial tumour, arteriovenous malformation or aneurysm;
8. Intracranial or spinal cord surgery within three months;
9. Gastrointestinal or urinary tract hemorrhage within the previous 21 days
10. Coagulation disorder, thrombocytopenia \<100, 000/mm3, and Prothrombin time INR ≥1.8
11. Index stroke is caused by infective endocarditis, dissection, systematic or central nervous system vasculitis
12. History of active malignancy being treated or life expectancy ≤ 90 days
13. Allergy to clopidogrel, ticagrelor or aspirin
14. Pregnancy or lactation
15. The presence of a major co-morbid illness that would make it unlikely that the participant will be able to complete follow-up
16. Conditional co-enrolment permitted except for ACT-42 trial (NoNO-42 Trial in Acute Ischemic Stroke).
